record.site_desc: The research site is located within the Barrow Environmental Observatory (BEO), a piece of native land set aside by the Ukpeagvik Iñupiat Corporation in 1973 specifically dedicated to conducting environmental research in Barrow, Alaska. The tower is positioned in a chain of aquatic habitats of polygonal tundra thaw ponds characterized by having a combination of vegetated and open-water areas. Aquatic emergent graminoids occupy the majority of the footprint along the littoral zone (e.g. Carex aquatilis) and inside (e.g. Arctophila fulva) these ponds. The tower is located in the center of a large drained thaw lake basin characterized by numerous thaw (peatland) ponds.

grp_igbp.igbp_comment: Vegetation composition is dominated by aquatic, seasonnaly flooded, and wet graminoid tundra based on Villareal et al (2012).
